File: `20260820120000_save_job_enforce_chem_unit_invariant_and_derive_totals.sql`, branch `claude/save-job-server-side-chem-unit`. **Apply order relative to rows 887-890 is unconstrained** — it shares no object with the draw-down candidates; it replaces the body of `public.save_job(uuid, jsonb, jsonb, jsonb, uuid, text)` and nothing else. `CREATE OR REPLACE` on the identical six-argument signature, so no overload is added and the existing `authenticated` / `service_role` EXECUTE grants are preserved; `SECURITY DEFINER` and `SET search_path = public, pg_temp` are carried through unchanged. Closes the standing review finding that the chemical-unit and money invariants were enforced **only in React**: EXECUTE is granted to `authenticated`, so a stale tab, a replayed request or a hand-built RPC call reached the old body directly, which took `total_cost_cents` / `total_price_cents` straight from `p_job_payload` with `COALESCE` and inserted `job_chemicals` without ever comparing `unit` against `rate_unit`. **Eight changes, nothing else.** (1) A chemical line whose units provably disagree is refused with `CHEM_UNIT_MISMATCH`, naming the product and both units — skip a row with no `product_id`, skip a zero quantity, refuse a billing line whose unit is blank (change 5), skip when the two units are equal, and treat `quantity = rate x acres` carried into the price's unit as the **only** proof of safety, at a tolerance that is now `GREATEST(0.0001, LEAST(0.00005 * acres, 0.1))` and reached that form through three corrections, all of them money bugs of one species — an allowance the CALLER gets to size. It was ORIGINALLY `GREATEST(0.0001, \|carried\| * 1e-6)`; round 18 removed the relative term because a per-million slack scales with the number it checks, so at 10,000 acres it permitted a 10-unit discrepancy. Round 23 widened it to `0.00005 * acres`, because a flat `0.0001` REFUSES the ordinary quantity-driven entry path — the app back-solves `rate = fmt4(quantity / acres)`, and a 4-decimal rate cannot reproduce the typed total. Round 24 capped that at `0.1`, because acreage is summed from caller-supplied `p_fields` and carries no CHECK anywhere in the live schema (verified against the live database 2026-08-24), so an uncapped acreage term is the round-18 bug reading a different number out of the same payload. Read the round-24 note below before trusting any tolerance description earlier in this row. (2) A rate measured per something other than acres is refused with `CHEM_RATE_DENOMINATOR_NOT_ACRES` in the slash form (`oz/cwt`), the spelled-out form (`oz per cwt`) and the hyphenated form (`oz-per-cwt`); the per-acre exclusion is plural-tolerant on both sides, so `gal per acres` still saves. (3) A quantity that is negative, `NaN` or `Infinity` is refused with `CHEM_QUANTITY_NOT_FINITE` **before** the unit comparison and regardless of its outcome, because it reaches the money totals whether or not the units agree. (4) `total_cost_cents` / `total_price_cents` are derived from `p_chemicals` via `safe_cents_qty` (exact `numeric`, `ROUND` half away from zero, applied per line then summed, `customer_supplied` contributing 0) and the caller-supplied totals are ignored — which is what makes a stale tab harmless. The derivation is byte-for-concept identical to what `transfer_job_to_invoice` already bills, so the stored job header and the invoice agree by construction. (5) A chemical line that actually bills but whose rate unit or stock `unit` is blank is refused with `CHEM_UNIT_UNSPECIFIED` — the round-6 policy change described below; `customer_supplied` lines, lines carrying neither a cost nor a price, and zero-quantity lines are exempt because they cannot bill wrongly. (6) The idempotency lookup routes through a canonical, advisory-locked helper instead of a raw unlocked `SELECT`, closing a pre-existing duplicate-job hole — the round-8 change described below. (7) That helper is `check_idempotency_intent(text, text, uuid, text)`, so the key is bound to the **calling actor** and to a **sha256 fingerprint of the request** (job id, job payload, fields and chemical lines, each array order-normalised before hashing) — the round-9 change described below. An unchanged retry still replays to the same job; another actor's receipt raises `IDEMPOTENCY_ACTOR_MISMATCH`; a changed payload on a spent key raises `IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH` instead of returning the earlier success while saving nothing. (b) The page and this function do **not** agree to the cent: `main` computes displayed totals with IEEE-754 binary multiply and half-up rounding, so the operator can see a figure one cent off what is stored until PR #436 lands the exact-cents client math. The line normalised to a plain `oz`, compared EQUAL to a stock `unit` of `oz`, and **saved**: a per-hundredweight rate billed as though it were per-acre, which is the exact money error the rule exists to stop. `oz per cwt per acre` was the same hole one spelling away. The test is now written **subtractively**: remove one trailing per-acre suffix in either spelling, then refuse if any `/` or whole-word `per` *survives*. That is strictly stronger and refuses nothing the exclusion form accepted — every legitimate spelling reduces to a bare unit, and a hyphenated unit such as `fl-oz` carries no separator to survive. `T24` and `T25` pin both stacked forms and a mutant reverting to the exclusion form turns `T24` red. **A latent defect in the prover itself was found in the same pass:** mutants were applied with `String.replace(from, to)`, and JavaScript treats `$&`, `` $` ``, `$'` and `$1` in a *string* replacement as substitution patterns — SQL regex literals here end in `$'` routinely, so such a mutant silently spliced the whole remainder of the migration into itself and failed to install with a syntax error far from the edit. The replacement now goes through a function and is taken verbatim. **Two further round-8 gate findings, one rejected on evidence and one accepted and still open.** *Rejected:* the gate reported that a clean replay cannot apply this migration because migration 20260215200000 leaves an undropped five-argument `save_job` overload. That premise is false — migration `20260331600000` (the RPC-overload consolidation) collects every `save_job` overload, **drops all of them**, and recreates a single unified one, and each later migration (20260530020452, 20260609190820, 20260624120000, 20260706020000, 20260706080000) recreates the same six-argument signature; live carries exactly one overload, `pronargs` 6, read read-only 2026-08-24. Recorded as a disagreement rather than silently resolved. The same false premise had been repeated in this row at (δ) above, sourced from an earlier round, and is corrected there. *Accepted and now CLOSED, on Mason's 2026-08-24 scope decision:* `save_job` did its idempotency lookup with an unlocked `SELECT` scoped to `operation = 'save_job'` and recorded with `ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING`, while the live unique constraint is on `idempotency_key` **alone** (`idempotency_keys_idempotency_key_key`, verified live 2026-08-24). So a key already spent by another operation was invisible to the lookup, the mutation proceeded, the receipt insert was swallowed by the conflict, and the next retry mutated **again** — a duplicate job, and therefore a duplicate bill; two callers racing on one key could also both pass the unlocked lookup. That block was **byte-identical to the pre-change live body** (`20260706080000` lines 87–97 and 297–301), so it is a pre-existing defect this migration now closes rather than one it caused. The lookup routes through `check_idempotency(text, text)` — SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path` pinned, md5 `2c93efc82ad63c906eab944e8b70c88e`, already used by `draw_down_quote` and others — which takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on the key and raises `IDEMPOTENCY_CROSS_OP_KEY_REUSE`. **No grant change:** the helper is executable by `postgres` and `service_role` only, and `save_job` is SECURITY DEFINER owned by `postgres`, so the inner call runs with the owner's rights. Mason chose to fold this in rather than issue a follow-up migration, because a second migration replacing this same function body is the non-atomic hazard round 3 already caught. The tail `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING` is deliberately kept: a conflict can now only be a same-operation row, because cross-operation reuse raises before any mutation. `T26` pins the cross-operation refusal **and** that it wrote nothing, and `T27` pins that an ordinary same-key replay still returns the same job and creates no second one. The preflight additionally asserts the helper is installed (`PREFLIGHT_MISSING_HELPER`) — PL/pgSQL resolves the call at run time, so without that assertion a database lacking the helper would accept this migration cleanly and fail on the first real job save; a mutation phase drops the helper and requires the apply to abort. **Round-9 change — Mason's scope decision on 2026-08-24, taken on top of round 8 rather than deferred.** Round 8 stopped the *cross-operation* duplicate, but `check_idempotency(text, text)` matches on key and operation **only**, so a key already spent by an earlier `save_job` and then reused for a **different job or an edited payload** still returned the earlier success. That is the quieter half of the same defect: nothing is duplicated, but the current request is never saved and the operator is told it was — an edited quantity, cent amount or job header silently discarded. It also let any caller replay another user's receipt. The call now goes to `check_idempotency_intent(text, text, uuid, text)`, which additionally binds the **calling actor** and a **sha256 request fingerprint**. This is not a new helper written for this migration: it is installed live and already called by nine money RPCs — `create_return`, `approve_return`, `receive_return`, `reject_return`, `cancel_return`, `issue_return_credit`, `create_commission_payment`, `post_commission_payment`, `void_commission_payment` (read read-only from `pg_proc` 2026-08-24, md5 of the live body `edc73be809069669e8441eba7acf443d`). Four mechanics that a reader must not have to rediscover. (i) It returns a **wrapper** `{"found": true, "result": ...}`, not the bare result that `check_idempotency` returns, so the body unwraps `-> 'result'` and raises `IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_INVALID` on a receipt that is not an object carrying a `job_id`, rather than handing a malformed cached value back to the app. (ii) The fingerprint is hashed with `extensions.digest`, **schema-qualified on purpose**: pgcrypto lives in the `extensions` schema on this project while this body pins `search_path` to `public, pg_temp`, so an unqualified call would resolve at run time and fail on the first keyed save. The preflight asserts `extensions.digest(bytea, text)` exists for exactly that reason. (iii) Both `p_fields` and `p_chemicals` are order-normalised (`jsonb_agg(e ORDER BY e::text)`) before hashing, so a client that re-serialises the same grid in a different order still replays instead of being refused. (iv) The helper **fails closed** on a receipt carrying neither binding column — a pre-binding receipt's intent cannot be reconstructed, so it raises `IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH` rather than replaying blind; the receipt write therefore stamps `request_fingerprint` and `request_actor_id` and raises `IDEMPOTENCY_RECEIPT_MISSING` if that stamp lands on no row. The preflight gained three assertions accordingly: the helper, `extensions.digest`, and both receipt columns on `idempotency_keys` — all `PREFLIGHT_MISSING_HELPER`, all refusing the apply rather than deferring the failure to the first real job save. `T29` pins the actor mismatch (a seeded receipt bound to a different actor is refused and writes nothing), `T30` pins A→B→A payload reuse (the changed payload is refused, and the original payload still replays to the same job), and two mutants pin the code: reverting to the key-only helper turns `T30` red, and dropping the receipt binding turns `T27` red. **A defect in the test suite was found by that second mutant and is worth recording**, because it is the same class as the round-7 postflight ordering bug — the prover found it, no reviewer did. With the receipt left unbound, the helper's fail-closed clause turns an *ordinary retry* into a hard `IDEMPOTENCY_INTENT_MISMATCH`; `T27` had no handler, so the whole test file aborted on a raw psql error and the mutation phase could not attribute the failure to any test. A mutant that fails the suite without failing its own test proves nothing. `T27` now carries the same `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` handler `T20` does, converting an outright refusal into a named `T27 FAIL`. **Round-10 change — a BLOCKER from the exact-SHA `gpt-5.6-sol` proof gate, and the second time this gate has caught a real money hole.** The unit guard could treat FLUID ounces as DRY ounces. `normalize_rate_unit` collapses `fl oz` to `oz` knowing nothing about the product, and the equality shortcut `CONTINUE WHEN v_qty_unit = v_price_unit` sat **above** the `product_form` lookup — so a DRY product carrying `rate_unit = 'fl oz/ac'` against a stock `unit` of `'oz'` normalised to `oz = oz`, took the shortcut, and billed with nothing proven. The alias is correct on a LIQUID product — the live `unit_conversions` table records `oz` as "alias for fl oz", both liquid, both factor 1 — but on a dry product `oz` is a dry ounce (a WEIGHT) while `fl oz` is a VOLUME, and `field_app_priced_quantity`, the authoritative converter the rest of the app bills through, **refuses the pair**: its dry branch sizes `fl oz` as NULL, i.e. not convertible. The guard was therefore **more lenient than the SQL that does the billing**, passing a shape its own converter calls unpriceable. An earlier round of this work had examined the same alias and cleared it — correctly, but only for liquids; the dry case was never checked, and that gap is why this is recorded rather than quietly fixed. **The fix is an ordering change plus a narrow refusal.** The `product_form` lookup moves ABOVE the shortcut, and a new `CHEM_UNIT_FORM_MISMATCH` fires only where the shortcut would otherwise have fired, only on a dry product, only when a fluid-ounce spelling is what made the two sides equal, and only when the two RAW spellings actually differ — because `field_app_priced_quantity` returns the quantity untouched whenever the raw units are identical, so `fl oz` against `fl oz` is self-consistent and must keep saving. **The wider form was considered and rejected**, and the reason is worth keeping: gating the shortcut on "the converter must agree" would refuse a LIQUID product priced in pounds (`lbs/ac` against `lb` normalise equal while the liquid size table carries no pound at all), and a false refusal blocks the WHOLE job save — the round-7 defect three reviewers caught. `T31` and `T32` pin both directions of the dry refusal, `T33` pins that the liquid pair still saves and `T34` that an identically-spelled dry pair still saves — the two false-refusal guards — and a mutant removing the rule turns `T31` red by name. **Reachability, stated at its real size:** no live product carries `fl oz` on a dry form today (read read-only 2026-08-24 — the 85 dry products use `dry oz`, `lb`, `mg` and `oz`), but the units compared here come from `p_chemicals`, not from the product catalog, and EXECUTE is granted to `authenticated`, so a hand-built call reaches the shape however clean the catalog is. Two OTHER findings the same gate raised in the round before were **rejected on evidence**: it reported that this branch rolls back the `codex-review` skill hardening and deletes the draw-tier real-schema prover. Both are artifacts of a stale base — the proof wrapper compares a snapshot of `origin/main` against a snapshot of HEAD, which is a two-dot comparison, so everything `main` gained since the merge base (PRs #448 and #442 here) reads as a rollback by the branch. The three-dot diff `origin/main...HEAD` is EMPTY for every file named, and merging current `origin/main` made both findings disappear. **Round-11 change — a second BLOCKER from the exact-SHA `gpt-5.6-sol` gate, and it reopened the round-8 rule.** The stacked-denominator refusal accepted a **MIXED-format** stack. The probe ran both strip patterns unconditionally, so `oz per acre/ac` — oz per acre PER ACRE, one denominator in each spelling — lost `/ac` to the slash pattern and then ` per acre` to the word pattern, came back a bare `oz` with nothing left to catch, normalised to `oz`, matched a stock `unit` of `oz` and **billed a per-acre-squared rate as if it were per-acre**. `oz-per-acre/ac` was the same hole one separator away. Round 8 had stated the rule correctly — "strip exactly one trailing per-acre suffix, then refuse if any denominator survives" — and then implemented two unconditional strips, which is a different rule: *remove one and refuse what survives* is not *remove every spelling and then look*. The second strip is now conditional on the first not having fired, which makes it singular as designed. `T35` and `T36` pin both mixed spellings and a mutant restoring the two unconditional passes turns `T35` red by name. The base derivation below the probe is deliberately left as split_part-plus-one-strip and is no longer claimed to be character-identical to the probe: anything reaching it has already been proved to carry at most one per-acre denominator in one spelling, because a stacked or mixed form is refused above and never arrives. **A MEDIUM from the same verdict was also fixed rather than argued down:** the container prover used a FIXED container name and ran `docker rm -f` on it before establishing that the container was its own, so a developer's unrelated container of that name would have been destroyed. The name is now unique per run, every container the prover starts carries a `crx.prover` label, and the only broad sweep filters on that label — nothing outside this prover can match. **Round-12 change — the round-10 fix was a HALF-fix, and the gate returned the other half as a fresh HIGH.** Round 10 made the fluid-ounce alias form-aware, but only at the **equality shortcut**. The shortcut is not the only way a fluid ounce reaches the money, and the path it missed is the worse one. `field_app_priced_quantity` is called with `v_qty_unit` and `v_price_unit` — the **NORMALISED** units — so `fl oz` has already become `oz` before the converter ever sees it. Handed the raw `fl oz` the converter's dry branch sizes it NULL and refuses; handed `oz` it sizes it 1 and converts **16:1 into pounds**. So a DRY product with `rate_unit = 'fl oz/ac'` against a stock `unit` of `'lb'` never took the shortcut at all — the two do not normalise equal — it went down the conversion path, turned a VOLUME into a WEIGHT, and derived the authoritative cost and price totals from it. Normalisation had erased the exact distinction the converter would have refused on. The rule is now **unconditional**: on a dry product, a fluid-ounce spelling on either side is refused, whatever the other side says and whether or not the two normalise equal. That is simpler as well as strictly stronger, and it has no precondition left to get wrong — a dry product has no density in this system, so nothing downstream can carry a fluid ounce into a weight honestly. **A test had to be INVERTED, and that is the part worth remembering.** Round 10's `T34` *required* a dry line quoted `fl oz` on both sides to SAVE, reasoning that identical spellings are self-consistent and the converter passes them untouched. Writing that exemption into a test **froze the half-fix in place** and would have defended it against the next reviewer. Self-consistent arithmetic on a unit the inventory and invoice sides cannot convert is not a saving grace. `T34` now asserts the refusal; `T37` (against `lb`) and `T38` (against `dry oz`) pin the conversion path the half-fix left open; `T33` still pins that the LIQUID `fl oz`/`oz` pair saves, which is the line that must not move; and the mutant that removes the rule now turns `T37` red — the conversion path — rather than `T31`. Proof re-run green at 44 behaviour tests and 24 mutation phases (18 turn a named test red, 6 abort the apply). **Round 15 (2026-08-24) closed three HIGH money findings from the exact-SHA gpt-5.6-sol gate, the first of which is the largest hole this file has carried.** (1) EQUAL UNITS WERE A FREE PASS FOR THE QUANTITY: the shortcut `CONTINUE WHEN v_qty_unit = v_price_unit` proved only that both sides were counted in the same unit and nothing about how many, so a hand-built call sending 10 acres at 2 oz/ac with quantity 200 oz passed and the derived totals authoritatively stored 20,000 cents instead of 2,000 — the caller setting the money directly, on the one path this migration exists to close. The mismatched branch already refused a quantity that is not `rate x acres`; applying that rule only when the units DIFFER was the inconsistency, since the quantity reaches the totals either way. The equal-units branch now derives `rate x acres` DIRECTLY, without calling the converter — the units are identical so no conversion is owed, and routing through it would make an exotic-but-self-consistent unit the tables do not carry (`cc` against `cc`) size NULL and start refusing a well-formed line. Verified read-only before the change that all three live BILLING rows satisfy `quantity = rate x acres` exactly (JOB-2026-0002 73.31 = 1 x 73.31; -0003 and -0004 3752.64 = 96 x 39.09), so this refuses nothing that exists; JOB-2026-0001 carries quantity 0 and is exempt earlier. `T42` pins it. A RESIDUAL is recorded rather than hidden: with no usable rate or acreage there is nothing to derive from, so such a line still saves on the caller's quantity — closing that means ruling a priced line with no acreage invalid, which is an operational policy call for Mason and is NOT taken here. (2) LEADING `per` FORMS evaded both the denominator and unspecified-unit guards, because every pattern required whitespace or a hyphen BEFORE `per`; `per cwt` therefore survived normalisation and, against a stock unit carrying the same text, reached the equality shortcut and billed. An earlier round had added this shape to the PRE-APPLY query but not to the runtime guard — fixing the report and leaving the enforcement, which is the half-fix pattern this file has now repeated three times. `T43` pins it. (3) HYPHENATED FLUID OUNCES bypassed the dry guard: the fold covered whitespace, periods and zero-width characters but not hyphens, so `fl-oz` on both sides of a dry line normalised equal and billed a volume as a weight. Third spelling escape in three rounds, which is why the fold now covers the separator class rather than the characters named so far. `T44` pins it. The prover also gained a structural fix worth more than any single mutant: an AMBIGUOUS mutation anchor is now refused outright unless the mutant opts into `all`. `String.replace` takes the first match, so when the acreage finiteness bound came to exist in two places the mutant silently edited the copy it did not mean, left the real guard standing, and the phase reported `MUTATION NOT DETECTED` — which reads as "this test is weak" and invites deleting a test that was simply never reached. **Round 16 (2026-08-24) ENDED THE CLASS rather than closing one more instance of it, and the table is the argument.** Four consecutive rounds of the dry fluid-ounce rule were defeated by a separator that had not been enumerated yet: round 12 (three literal spellings) by `fl. oz`; round 13 (+ periods and whitespace) by `fl<U+200B>oz`; round 14 (+ zero-width and NBSP) by `fl-oz`; round 15 (+ ASCII hyphen) by `fl<U+2010>oz`. U+2010 and U+2011 are hyphens and U+202F is a narrow no-break space, and Unicode carries many more — so enumeration could never converge, because the caller picks the character and the list is always written afterwards. The fold now has NO character list at all: everything that is not a letter or a digit is DELETED and what remains must BE the word (`floz`, `fluidounce`). No separator survives, so none can be smuggled in. Verified on live PostgreSQL 17.6 across 31 spellings — all 19 fluid-ounce forms refuse (every escape from rounds 12-15, plus `fl_oz` and `f l o z`), and all 12 legitimate units pass untouched including `dry oz`, `dry<NBSP>oz`, `dry-oz`, `gal.` and the near-miss `flour oz`, which folds to `flouroz` and fails the anchored `fl|fluid` prefix. `T45` pins U+2010, U+2011 and U+202F; a mutant narrowing the fold back to an ASCII list reddens `T45` ALONE while `T39`/`T40`/`T44` stay green, which is what makes the list-free property itself the thing under test rather than any one character. The NBSP reasoning recorded in round 14 is now moot and is marked as such in the migration: separation no longer matters, since `dry oz` folds to `dryoz` and simply fails the prefix. **Round 17 (2026-08-24) closed the UNDER-billing mirror of the round-15 finding, and settled the policy question both of them raised.** The gate found (HIGH) that the zero-quantity exit was UNCONDITIONAL: a line with a real price, a real rate and real acreage but `quantity = 0` saved and billed NOTHING, and the zero propagated into the invoice. Where the equality shortcut let a caller OVER-charge, this let one UNDER-charge. It also found that `T20` encoded the defect as correct behaviour — it submitted 10 acres at 1.5 pt/ac with a price and quantity 0 and required the total to stay 0 — the second test in this file written around a defect that would have defended it against the next reviewer. **Mason's decision (2026-08-24): refuse only where a customer's money is actually at stake.** Implemented as two refusals and three exemptions. `CHEM_QUANTITY_ZERO_BUT_EXPECTED` refuses a zero-quantity line that carries a PRICE when a positive quantity was derivable; `CHEM_QUANTITY_UNVERIFIABLE` refuses a priced line whose quantity cannot be checked at all — which closes the bypass round 15 left open, where a hand-built call could switch the entire check off by simply OMITTING the rate and naming any quantity (a guard the caller can disable is not a guard). The three exemptions are each a case where zero is genuinely right: `customer_supplied` (contributes 0 by definition); NO PRICE (nothing can be under-charged — this is what keeps live JOB-2026-0001 saveable, since it carries quantity 0 against a 5/ac rate over 178.31 acres with a cost but price 0, and `T47` pins that shape); and NO usable rate or acreage (nothing was EXPECTED, which is the ordinary-UI path `T20` exists for, where a product is picked before any acreage is entered — there acres = 0 so the expected quantity is 0 too). `T20` was corrected to carry acres 0, the scenario it was always about. A recorded, accepted residual: a cost-only line (price 0) can still misstate MARGIN through an unverified quantity, which follows directly from conditioning on price. `T46` pins the underbilling refusal, `T48` the unverifiable-quantity refusal, `T47` the live-shape exemption, and each has a mutant reddening its own test. The prover also gained an AMBIGUOUS-ANCHOR check in round 15 that earned its keep immediately here: three mutants had anchors that this round made non-unique or stale, and each was refused loudly instead of silently editing the wrong site and reporting a good test as weak. **Round 18 (2026-08-24) closed two more HIGH money findings, one of which is the subtlest in the file.** (1) THE QUANTITY TOLERANCE WAS A PERCENTAGE. Both comparison sites allowed `GREATEST(0.0001, |expected| * 1e-6)` -- one part per million. Nothing bounds rate, acreage or quantity, so that is not a small amount: it is a fraction of whatever the caller chose. At 5,000 acres and a rate of 1e9 the accepted difference is 5,000,000 units, i.e. a $5,000,000 discrepancy at $1 a unit, waved through by a rule whose stated purpose was rounding. It is now a FIXED `0.0001` at both sites -- exactly the precision `fmt4` stores the quantity at, and nothing more. `T50` pins that a 5-unit shortfall on a 10,000,000-unit line is refused; `T51` pins that a genuine 0.0001 rounding difference on that same line still SAVES, because over-tightening a money guard is its own defect. A side effect worth recording: the fixed tolerance independently closes the NaN-acreage bypass, since `abs(v_qty - NaN) <= 0.0001` is FALSE where `NaN <= GREATEST(0.0001, NaN)` was TRUE. The finiteness-bound mutant had to restore BOTH halves to reproduce the original defect, and the prover refused to score a detection it had not earned until it did -- two independent guards now stand between a NaN acreage and the money. (2) DENOMINATOR SEPARATORS WERE ENUMERATED, the same defect that beat the fluid-ounce rule four times, in the per-acre rule: it looked for `per` bounded by whitespace or hyphens, so `oz_per_cwt` and `oz.per.cwt` matched nothing, survived normalisation, and with a stock `unit` carrying the same text reached the equality branch and billed a PER-HUNDREDWEIGHT rate as per-acre. Separators are now folded to single spaces before the denominator is classified (`/` deliberately preserved, since there it is the denominator marker rather than a separator), after which the existing subtractive logic runs against exactly one spelling. The canonical form also subsumes the leading-`per` arm added in round 15, so that arm was REMOVED rather than left as a second way of saying the same thing. `T49` pins both spellings; every existing denominator test (`T13`, `T24`, `T25`, `T35`, `T36`, `T43`) and both legitimate per-acre tests (`T5`, `T10`) stay green. That is the third distinct place in this file where enumerating characters failed, which is a pattern rather than three coincidences. **Round 19 (2026-08-24) closed an ASYMMETRY in the fluid-ounce rule (HIGH) and bound the audit identity to the idempotency key (MEDIUM).** (1) The rate side reached the fluid-ounce check already stripped of its denominator (`v_rate_base`), but the stock side was passed in RAW. A dry line with `rate_unit = 'oz/ac'` against a stock `unit` of `'fl oz/ac'` therefore folded to `flozac`, missed the anchored pattern, and `normalize_rate_unit` then collapsed BOTH sides to `oz` anyway -- so the equality branch accepted it and derived authoritative money from a VOLUME price on a weight product. The defect was the asymmetry itself: two sides of one comparison were being canonicalised differently. `'fl oz/ac'` still DENOTES fluid ounces -- a denominator says per what, not what -- so each side is now reduced to the unit it names before the concept test runs: fold separators (keeping `/` meaningful), drop everything from the first `/`, drop a spelled-out `per ...` tail, then delete every remaining non-alphanumeric. Verified on live PostgreSQL 17.6 across 21 spellings: all 8 fluid-ounce forms refuse including `fl oz/ac`, `fl oz per acre`, `fluid ounce per acre`, `fl-oz/ac` and `fl.oz/ac`, while every legitimate unit passes untouched including the denominator forms `oz/ac`, `lb/ac`, `gal/ac`, `pt/ac`, `dry oz/ac` and the near-miss `flour oz/ac`. `T52` pins it. (2) `p_performed_by` was missing from the idempotency fingerprint although it is written to `jobs.created_by`. The actor check only refuses that parameter when it is non-NULL AND disagrees with the caller, so flipping it between NULL and the authenticated actor passes the check while changing what the row records -- and on a spent key the earlier receipt replayed, silently discarding the new audit identity. That is the identical silent-discard shape round 9 fixed for the payload, missed here because this parameter is not part of the payload. It is now fingerprinted separately from `v_actor`, because it is a different input with a different effect. `T53` pins it. **Two mutants had to be strengthened rather than the code weakened**, both for the same reason and both caught by the prover refusing to score an unearned detection: the round-19 denominator-stripping wrapper carries its OWN list-free fold, so narrowing only the outer fold left Unicode separators still handled (`T45` stayed green until the mutant narrowed both), and the round-18 fixed tolerance independently closes the NaN-acreage path (`T11` stayed green until the mutant restored the relative tolerance too). In both cases two independent guards now stand between the defect and the money. **Round 20 (2026-08-24) ended the separator-bypass class for the DENOMINATOR rule, and disproved a BLOCKER.** The gate raised two items. The first was a BLOCKER claiming this branch had replaced the proof generator's fixed Git executable and isolated environment with ambient `execFileSync("git", ...)`, dropped `--no-replace-objects`, and deleted the hostile-global-config regression test -- i.e. that a future packet could be steered by untrusted Git state to mint a clean proof for unreviewed code. **It is a FALSE POSITIVE from a stale base, and the three-dot diff disproves it in one command:** `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- scripts/write-codex-push-proof.mjs` is EMPTY, so this branch never touched the file. `origin/main` had gained 3 commits since the merge base, one of which HARDENED that very file, and the review packet compares snapshots -- structurally a two-dot diff -- so main's own improvement renders as "the candidate deleted this". Resolved by MERGING `origin/main`, not by editing anything; hand-restoring a security-critical file to match a version never read is how the warned-about vulnerability would actually get introduced. This is the documented trap recorded in the branch handoff, and it has now produced three confident false BLOCKERS across this work. The second finding was REAL (HIGH): the denominator canon preserves ASCII `/` and folds every other punctuation mark to a space, so `oz<U+2215>cwt` -- a Unicode DIVISION SLASH -- became `oz cwt` with no `/` and no whole-word `per` surviving, and a PER-HUNDREDWEIGHT rate would bill as per-acre. Rather than add slash homoglyphs to a list -- which would have been the FIFTH round of the game the fluid-ounce list lost four times -- the question changed. What separates `oz cwt` from a legitimate `fl oz` is not the character between the words, it is that `oz cwt` IS NOT A UNIT. A priced line must now name a unit the system recognises: either `normalize_rate_unit` maps it to a canonical unit (`oz`, `pt`, `qt`, `gal`, `lb`, `ton`, `g`, `kg`, `l`, `ml`) or the folded spelling exists in the live `unit_conversions` table. A denominator smuggled in behind ANY separator, including ones not yet invented, leaves a residue that is not a unit and is refused. Gated on PRICE per Mason's 2026-08-24 rule; the recorded residual is unchanged (a cost-only line can still misstate margin), and live JOB-2026-0001 carries `rate_unit` `'32'` with price 0 and stays saveable for exactly that reason. `T54` pins three homoglyphs (U+2215, U+2044, U+FF0F); `T55` pins that all six live unit spellings still SAVE on a priced line, and it is deliberately built so that BOTH arms of the rule are load-bearing -- `dry oz` survives only via `unit_conversions` (no `normalize_rate_unit` arm) and `ton` only via the canonical-output arm (no `unit_conversions` row). The harness gained a `unit_conversions` table mirroring the live 11 spellings, because a proof against a different allowlist would prove nothing about production. **Round 21 (2026-08-24) is the most instructive round in this file: the FOLD ITSELF was doing the attacker's work.** The gate submitted `oz<U+2215>сԝт` — a Unicode division slash followed by CYRILLIC homoglyphs for `cwt`. Under `[^a-z0-9]` every non-ASCII character is DELETED, so that string folds to a clean `oz`. The denominator was not caught, it was ERASED; `oz` is a perfectly recognised unit, both sides matched, and a per-hundredweight rate would bill as per-acre. **Every separator round from 12 to 20 rested on the assumption that folding leaves a residue behind for a rule to catch. Against non-ASCII it leaves nothing.** The fold may no longer discard anything silently: a small enumerated set is normalised first (Unicode spaces to a space, zero-width deleted) and ANY remaining character outside `[a-z0-9 ./-]` refuses a priced line with `CHEM_UNIT_UNSUPPORTED_CHARACTER`. The property that matters is the inversion — **the enumeration is for CONVENIENCE and the allowlist is for SAFETY**, so getting the convenience list wrong can only cause a REFUSAL, never an acceptance. That is the opposite of rounds 12-20, where an incomplete list meant something slipped through, and it is why this round ends the class rather than closing one more instance. Ordering is deliberate: it sits AFTER the fluid-ounce rule so a dry line written `fl<U+2010>oz` still reports the specific `CHEM_UNIT_FORM_MISMATCH` that tells the operator what is actually wrong. Measured on live PostgreSQL 17.6, the round-13 expression missed five real forms: `fl<ZWSP>oz`, `fl<ZWNJ>oz`, `fl<ZWJ>oz`, `fl<BOM>oz`, `fluid<ZWSP> ounce`. Zero-width is DELETED (it separates nothing, so `fl<ZWSP>oz` must close to `floz`) while the non-breaking space is MAPPED TO A SPACE (it does separate, so `dry<NBSP>oz` must stay two words) — `T40` pins the refusal, `T41` pins that the legitimate `dry<NBSP>oz` line still SAVES, and a mutant removing only the zero-width fold turns `T40` red while leaving `T39` and `T41` green. The pre-apply count gained a fourth term (a rate that is only a denominator, `per acre`/`per-acre`, which the earlier strip could not reduce to empty) and now carries an explicit SCOPE note: it mirrors the `CHEM_UNIT_UNSPECIFIED` refusal ONLY, so a zero there is not a claim about the other four refusals. Verified on live PostgreSQL 17.6 over 23 spellings: all 13 fluid-ounce forms refuse, and `oz`, `dry oz`, `lb`, `ton`, `mg`, `gal`, `pt` and the near-miss `flour oz` do not. `T39` pins the refusal, `T34` (no periods) and `T33` (the LIQUID false-refusal guard) both stay green, and a dedicated mutant that removes **only** the period folding turns `T39` red while leaving `T34` green. **Round 22 (2026-08-24) records the LIMIT OF THE WHOLE FILE, and pins a live row.** Every guard in this migration checks that units are INTERNALLY CONSISTENT; not one checks that a rate is PLAUSIBLE. All twenty-one rounds of hardening pass it and the invoice comes out roughly six orders of magnitude low. It is now a banner block in the migration header so nobody reads the file's length as coverage of that question -- closing it needs per-product plausible-rate bounds, which is separate work. It is the only test exercising three things together that nothing else touches: the NULL-form branch every form-aware rule collapses into "not dry", a unit typed `both` in `unit_conversions` so neither the liquid nor the dry table settles it, and the units-equal path where no conversion can occur. If `T58` ever goes red, that product has stopped being sellable. **Round 23 (2026-08-24) stopped the guard REFUSING ordinary work, and round 24 stopped the fix being a new hole — the two are one lesson and are recorded together.** The gate found (HIGH) that the flat `0.0001` tolerance breaks the quantity-driven entry path. The app supports two directions: enter a RATE and it fills `quantity = fmt4(rate x acres)`, or enter a QUANTITY and it HOLDS that total and back-solves `rate_per_acre = fmt4(quantity / acres)`. `buildJobChemicalsPayload` does not send which direction was used, so the server cannot tell them apart and must accept both — and the second cannot reproduce `quantity = rate x acres`, because the rate it stores has been rounded to four decimals. The gate's ordinary job: 178.31 acres, operator types 10, the UI stores rate 0.0561, and `0.0561 x 178.31 = 10.003191` — off by 0.003191, which a flat 0.0001 refuses, and one refused line rolls back the WHOLE job save. That is the round-7 defect reached by TIGHTENING rather than loosening, and `T51` missed it because `T51` tests the rate-driven direction only. Round 23 sized the slack as the rate's own rounding error, `0.00005 * acres`. **Round 24 (2026-08-24) then caught that as a fresh HIGH from the same gate, and the reasoning is the part worth keeping.** The round-23 commit message defended the new term by asserting acreage is "physically bounded by the field". THE SERVER DOES NOT KNOW THAT: acreage is summed out of `p_fields`, which the caller writes, and no CHECK constrains it anywhere in the live schema. The gate's arithmetic — 1e12 acres at a rate of 1e-9 expects 1,000 units and opens a slack of 50,000,000, so a submitted quantity of 50,001,000 passes and every one of them bills. A caller-sized allowance is exactly what round 18 deleted; round 23 rebuilt it out of a different field. The fix is an ABSOLUTE ceiling — `LEAST(..., 0.1)` — on both comparison sites, converted through `field_app_priced_quantity` on the mismatched-units branch so the cap is the same PHYSICAL amount on either side (0.1 gal is 12.8 oz) rather than the same digits. Five findings were accepted and fixed rather than waived:
> * **Silent-clobber on replay** — the md5 skip branch in `20260813020000` now pins both ends; see row 873.
> * **Half-proven probe safety** — the trigger enumeration guarding the probe covered `INSERT` only while the probe also has an `UPDATE` leg, so a future unscoped `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger could have overwritten the rounded values with every assertion still passing. It now enumerates `INSERT` *or* `UPDATE` against the five siblings read from live `pg_trigger` on 2026-08-10 (`trg_stamp_commission_split_recipient_ids`, `enforce_order_status_transition`, `guard_order_customer_source_lineage`, `guard_order_delivered_activity_cancel`, `trg_order_status_change`), every one of them column-scoped to `status`, `customer_id`, `commission_split` or `deleted_at` and therefore unable to touch the money columns.
> * **Undisclosed sign laundering** — because the rounding trigger is `BEFORE`, it runs ahead of CHECK evaluation, so a `total_price` in `(-0.005, 0)` now rounds to `0.00` and passes `orders_total_price_non_negative` where it previously raised. Under one cent, judged acceptable, and now stated in the file rather than left implicit.
> * **Self-contradicting re-runnability claim** — `20260813030000` claimed "no window in which bad data could be written" while arguing 100 lines earlier that the applier must not be assumed to wrap the file in a transaction. The claim is corrected to state the window precisely (nil on first apply; open only on a retry against a database that already carries the constraints). An explicit `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` was **rejected**: if the applier has already opened a transaction, the inner `COMMIT` would commit *its* transaction early and split the migration, a worse failure than the one it would prevent.
> * **Name-only constraint lookup** — section 3 of `20260813030000`'s post-condition matched seven pre-existing whole-cent constraints on `conname` alone while sections 1 and 2 pin the table, failing the file's own stated standard. It now derives the table from the constraint-name prefix and also requires `contype = 'c'`.
